models_evaluated: AI clinical decision support solution for intracranial hemorrhage detection

links.outcome: AI performance and read time in high-volume, low-prevalence teleradiology setting
links.effect: Prevalence 2.70%, PPV 21.1%; falsely flagged exams took mean 9:40 vs 8:25 pre-AI and 8:38 post-AI unflagged (P<.001), so inefficiencies may outweigh benefits.
links.quote: With lengthened read times for falsely flagged examinations, system inefficiencies may outweigh the potential benefits of using the tool in a high volume, low prevalence environment.

links.outcome: Radiologist read times for AI-flagged false positive exams versus baseline
links.effect: False-flagged no-bleed exams averaged 9 min 40 s (median 8:07) vs 8 min 25 s pre-AI (n=49,007) and 8:38 for unflagged post-AI (n=52,281), P<.001.
links.quote: Of the 56 745 post-AI CT scans with no bleed identified by a radiologist, examinations falsely flagged as suspected ICH by the AI solution (n = 4464) took an average of 9 minutes 40 seconds (median, 8 minutes 7 seconds) to interpret as compared with 8 minutes 25 seconds (median, 6 minutes 48 seconds) for unremarkable CT scans before AI (n = 49 007) (P < .001) and 8 minutes 38 seconds (median, 6 minutes 53 seconds) after AI when ICH was not suspected by the AI solution (n = 52 281) (P < .001).

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance of AI for ICH in a real-world teleradiology practice
links.effect: Sensitivity 75.6%, specificity 92.1%, accuracy 91.7%, prevalence 2.70%, PPV 21.1% across 61,704 exams.
links.quote: The AI solution had a sensitivity of 75.6%, specificity of 92.1%, accuracy of 91.7%, prevalence of 2.70%, and positive predictive value of 21.1%.

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and workflow impact (radiologist interpretation time) before and after deployment of a deep learning tool for ICH detection in a national teleradiology program, without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice variation.
